sections.h2: How does a deed get recorded in Geauga County?
sections.html:
A Geauga County deed passes through three offices in Chardon, and the county publishes a one-page reference sheet effective June 30, 2026 that lays out the order. The County Engineer approves the legal description, the County Auditor transfers the parcel and collects the conveyance fee, and the County Recorder records the document and returns it.

Geauga County is in the northeast corner of Ohio, part of the Cleveland metropolitan area, and Chardon is the county seat. The county was founded on March 1, 1806, as the second county in the Connecticut Western Reserve, and its first settlement was at Burton in 1798.

sections.h2: What does each of the three Chardon offices handle?
sections.html:
The reference sheet lists the three stops, their addresses and what each one needs from you.

  • County Engineer, 12665 Merritt Rd, Chardon, phone (440) 279-1800: reviews the legal description and stamps it with an original (wet) stamp. No fee. Allow 2 to 3 business days. Bring a legible copy of the prior deed with its volume and page reference.
  • County Auditor, 231 Main St, Suite 1-A, phone (440) 279-1600: transfers the property and updates the tax records. Needs the original signed and notarized deed.
  • County Recorder, 231 Main St, Suite 1-C, phone (440) 279-2020: records the deed and mails the original back.

The Recorder's page puts the Auditor two doors down the hall. A deed sent by mail goes with a short cover letter and phone number, a stamped return envelope, and two checks: one to the Recorder and one to the Auditor.

sections.h2: What does the Geauga County Auditor charge to transfer a deed?
sections.html:
The Auditor charges $4.00 per $1,000 of transfer value and $0.50 per parcel, and checks for both are made payable to the Geauga County Auditor. The Recorder's FAQ also puts the conveyance fee at four dollars per thousand and refers fee questions to the Auditor.

Ohio law explains the split. The first layer is the statement-of-value fee in R.C. 319.54(G)(3), ten cents on each hundred dollars. The second is a county tax capped at thirty cents per hundred under R.C. 322.02, which the grantor pays to the Auditor ahead of recording. Gifts between spouses or from a parent to a child, transfers with no consideration and some trust transfers are exempt under the statute.

The Recorder asks for a completed DTE 100 or DTE 100EX conveyance form with the deed. A Transfer on Death Affidavit is the exception the Recorder names: it has no Auditor fee.

sections.h2: How much does the Geauga County Recorder charge?
sections.html:
State law fixes the Recorder's charge at $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each page that follows. The office returns documents unrecorded when the check is short or too high, so match the fee to the page count before you mail it.

sections.h2: Can I record a Geauga County deed electronically?
sections.html:
The reference sheet says electronic recording of conveyances is available and lets you skip the paper steps, and the 2026 sheet also says legal descriptions presented that way do not need the wet Engineer stamp. An older Recorder page still says eRecording is not available for any document that needs conveyance through the Auditor, so call (440) 279-2020 to confirm what the office will take.

Paper filings are on a fast clock. The Recorder's FAQ gives same-day turnaround, and an electronic recording is returned when it is recorded. Leave a self-addressed stamped envelope with an in-person deed, or come back the next day to pick it up.

sections.h2: What are the Geauga County Recorder's document rules?
sections.html:
The sheet lists what each deed needs before it reaches the counter.

  • Legible signatures, and printed names under any that are hard to read.
  • The name of the person who prepared the document.
  • Notary acknowledgments for each grantor.
  • Original wet stamps from the Engineer and the Auditor.
  • The 8-digit permanent parcel numbers.
  • A completed conveyance form.

The extra $20 for a non-standard document comes from R.C. 317.114, which asks for ten point type, black or blue ink and a blank three inch strip at the top of page one. The Recorder's office does not give legal advice, cannot notarize, and does not run title searches, since state law bars it. The Recorder stopped accepting Torrens registered land filings, and it does not sell blank forms.

sections.h2: What else does the Geauga County Recorder keep for owners and sellers?
sections.html:
The Recorder's FAQ answers the questions that come up around a sale. Geauga County has no tract (geographical) indexing, and only the indexes of recorded documents are online, so a full copy of an old deed means a copy request. Copies made by the public cost ten cents a page, while a copy made with staff help is two dollars a page.

  • Releases and assignments do not need a legal description, but they do carry the $4.00 marginal notation fee.
  • Soldier discharge records (DD214) are recorded, and a recorded discharge is what the office uses to issue a Veterans ID card.
  • Blank forms are not sold. The office suggests an office supply store, a title company or an attorney.
  • The office will not search the title for you, and it will not notarize or give legal advice.

A shortage or overage on the check sends the document back unrecorded, so call (440) 279-2020 with the page count if you are unsure.

sections.h2: What do Geauga County's housing numbers look like to a seller?
sections.html:
The 2020 Census put Geauga's population at 95,397, and the July 2025 estimate is 95,676. Owners hold 87.2 percent of the housing, a typical owned home is valued at $331,100, and the median household earns $107,860. The county issued 180 building permits in 2025.

The county covers about 400 square miles of land and is the headwaters of the Cuyahoga, Chagrin and Grand rivers. Most of it gets over 42 inches of precipitation in an average year, the most of any county in northern Ohio, which makes drainage and basement condition worth a look before you list.

Chardon, Burton, Middlefield, South Russell and Hunting Valley are the municipalities, and the townships include Bainbridge, Munson, Russell and Newbury. In November 2024 voters dissolved the Village of Aquilla, and a transition board oversees the change.

faqs.q: What are the total charges to record a deed in Geauga County?
faqs.a: Expect $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 per extra page at the Recorder, with $20.00 more for a non-standard deed. The Auditor bills $4.00 per $1,000 of value and $0.50 per parcel on its own.

faqs.q: Do I need the County Engineer for a Geauga County deed?
faqs.a: Yes, for paper filings. The Engineer reviews and approves the legal description with an original stamp at no fee, usually within 2 to 3 business days. Legal descriptions sent through electronic recording are the exception.

faqs.q: Where is the Geauga County Recorder located?
faqs.a: Find it at 231 Main Street, Suite 1-C, Chardon, Ohio 44024, or ring (440) 279-2020. The County Auditor is in Suite 1-A of the same building.

faqs.q: Will the Recorder search the title to my house?
faqs.a: No. The Recorder's FAQ says state law prohibits the office from doing title searches. Use the online index of recorded documents, a title company or an attorney instead.

faqs.q: How long does recording take in Chardon?
faqs.a: The Recorder lists a same-day turnaround. Mailed deeds come back to you after recording in the self-addressed stamped envelope you include, and an electronic recording is returned when it is recorded.
